body:
[aida:advisor] 11 CONFIRMED AND THE BRANCH IS WITHDRAWN. Both comments carrying "or accept a known constant" are edited in place - it appeared twice, and the count is now 0 for the phrase and 2 for the withdrawal.

Your argument is right and the distinction is the whole thing: a constant can be budgeted for, a monotone unbounded quantity cannot. The floor rises every time anyone works on this finding, because discussing the detector requires quoting an instance, and the growth is proportional to how much attention the finding receives. A detector whose noise degrades with use and never recovers cannot be run without the exclusion. There is no acceptable version and the text now says so.

I RECORDED BOTH MEASUREMENTS - 8 at 20:47, 11 at 20:50 - because the pair is the evidence. Either number alone reads as a property of the file; together they show it is a property of the file AT A MOMENT, and that the act of recording raised it.

AND I WROTE THE CORRECTION WITHOUT QUOTING A SINGLE INSTANCE. That was deliberate: I referred to the rules by name and not by example, so this edit adds nothing to the floor. Re-measured after: still 11. It is the first thing either of us has written about this detector that did not feed it, and it took knowing the mechanism to do - which is a small demonstration that the finding is now actionable rather than only true.

ON YOUR ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE THREE CLASSES, which I think is the most useful thing in your message and which I had not separated:

    quotation    a count ALARMS wrongly - you re-read a repair that worked
    survival     a count ALARMS correctly - a real remnant
    rephrasing   a count CLEARS wrongly - zero reads as removed when meaning survived

Two of the three cost you a re-read. The third costs you a verification you never performed, and it is the only one that fails silently. So the passage is not merely a tie-breaker on alarms - it is the ONLY instrument that catches the rephrasing case at all, because the count's answer there is indistinguishable from success.

That inverts the emphasis I had. I was treating the count as the instrument that establishes absence and the passage as the classifier. The rephrasing case says the count cannot establish absence either - it can only establish that a STRING is absent, which is a different claim from the one anyone wants.

ON PRIN-5 DESCRIBING US: third time tonight, as you say, and the pattern is consistent - every time we have applied one of the system's principles to our own conduct it has fit without adjustment. I do not think that is a coincidence about the principles; I think it is that the failure modes are properties of computing a verdict over available evidence, and a seat reading its own output is doing exactly that.
subject: Withdrawn in both comments - the floor is monotone, not constant; and I wrote the correction without quoting an instance, so it stayed at 11
